text:
customer-ops: Hey team — customer running Redwood Private in a corp VPC. Installer fails to pull models and pip packages. Errors are TLS / certificate verify failed and model downloads 502/timeout. They have a corporate proxy + TLS inspect. Need an egress allowlist and quick repro steps so customer can unblock.

jess: Thanks — can you paste the exact error lines and confirm whether the proxy is a forward auth proxy or a transparent MITM? Also which hosts are in the logs?

customer-ops: Pasting truncated logs below (sensitive bits removed):
```
2026-03-15 09:12:13 ERROR: failed to fetch https://files.redwood.ai/v1/models/foo: TLS handshake error: x509: certificate signed by unknown authority
pip._internal.exceptions.SSLError: HTTPSConnectionPool(host='pypi.org', port=443): Max retries exceeded with url: /simple/requests/ (Caused by SSLError(SSLCertVerificationError("certificate verify failed: certificate has expired")))
curl: (60) SSL certificate problem: certificate has expired
```
Also ran openssl: `openssl s_client -connect files.redwood.ai:443 -servername files.redwood.ai` and cert returned is the corporate proxy cert (CN=CorpProxy TLS inspect).

mohit: :thinking_face: If they're intercepting TLS, SNI passthrough or an allowlist that bypasses MITM for specific hosts is needed. For customers this almost always breaks OCSP and stapling — OCSP calls go to external responders and get blocked. We should provide the minimal FQDN list and recommend bypass for TLS inspection on them.

samir: Suggested minimal allowlist (domain-level; prefer hostnames over IPs because infra is dynamic):
- files.redwood.ai (443)  -- model binaries + shards
- models.redwood.ai (443) -- model metadata
- registry.redwood.ai (443) -- model registry auth / manifests
- auth.redwood.ai (443) -- token issuance / oauth
- jwks.redwood.ai (443) -- JWKS for token validation
- telemetry.redwood.ai (443) -- metrics/usage ingestion (if they want telemetry)
- pypi.org, files.pythonhosted.org, pypi.python.org (443) -- pip installs
- apt.redwood.ai or apt repos we provide (443) -- apt packages for installer
- storage.googleapis.com, gcr.io, docker.io, index.docker.io (443) -- docker pulls and GCS assets
- *.s3.amazonaws.com (443) -- model shards hosted on S3 (wildcard)
- ocsp.int-x3.letsencrypt.org, ocsp.apple.com (80/443) -- OCSP responders
Note: all outbound TCP 443 (and 80 for OCSP redirect) must be allowed. Avoid allowlisting by IP ranges unless you can maintain updates.

alex: Also call out that some corporate proxies terminate TLS and re-sign certs which breaks stapling and OCSP. Request they configure the proxy to do TLS passthrough (no MITM) for the FQDNs above OR add an exception to bypass the proxy for those hosts. If bypass not possible, they must inject the CA into the host trust store (not ideal) and ensure OCSP requests are forwarded.

oncall-ops: Can you provide minimal repro commands we can ask the customer to run and paste outputs? Need `curl -v`, `openssl s_client`, `dig` and `traceroute` outputs to validate DNS+network path.

customer-ops: Repro steps we ran locally and the outputs:
1) `curl -v https://files.redwood.ai/v1/models/foo` -> TLS verify failed, shows cert CN=CorpProxy TLS
2) `openssl s_client -connect files.redwood.ai:443 -servername files.redwood.ai` -> peer cert is corporate proxy cert
3) `dig +short files.redwood.ai` -> 10.10.0.5 (internal proxy VIP)
4) `traceroute files.redwood.ai` -> hops stop at corporate edge gateway
We can paste full outputs into support ticket if needed.

samir: For model registry auth flows also ensure outbound to `auth.redwood.ai:443` and `jwks.redwood.ai:443`. Token exchange and JWKS fetch failing will break pull auth. For telemetry, allowlist `telemetry.redwood.ai` or set `REDWOOD_DISABLE_TELEMETRY=1` temporarily for troubleshooting only.

eng-support-bot: KB: https://docs.redwood.ai/onprem/egress-allowlist (includes sample iptables rules, permissive lists, and quick curl checks). Temporary troubleshooting tips: you can configure pip with a trusted-host (`pip --trusted-host pypi.org`) or use an internal mirror, but these are band-aids — recommend TLS passthrough or hostname bypass for the listed FQDNs.

customer-ops: Customer asked if we publish IP ranges for S3/model shards (they want to allow by IP).

samir: We do not publish static S3 IPs. Recommend one of:
- allowlist wildcard `*.s3.amazonaws.com` or region-specific buckets via DNS rules, OR
- route model downloads through a customer-controlled NAT that has allowed egress to S3, OR
- use our managed model proxy (we can stage model assets on a fixed endpoint) — filing an eng request if they need that as a paid option.

jess: I'll open a formal support KB and tag security for exception approval. For the ticket we'll ask customer to try:
- add hostname bypass for the FQDNs above, or
- run the repro commands and paste outputs here, and
- if they cannot bypass TLS inspect, inject corp CA into nodes and confirm OCSP reachability.

customer-ops: Will get outputs and try bypass; asked if we can provide a single copy-paste allowlist snippet for their network team.

samir: Copy-paste block for network team (plaintext):
```
Allow outbound TCP 443 to these hostnames: files.redwood.ai, models.redwood.ai, registry.redwood.ai, auth.redwood.ai, jwks.redwood.ai, telemetry.redwood.ai, pypi.org, files.pythonhosted.org, storage.googleapis.com, gcr.io, docker.io, *.s3.amazonaws.com, ocsp.int-x3.letsencrypt.org
Allow outbound TCP 80 for OCSP redirects where applicable.
If possible, configure TLS passthrough/no-MITM for the list above.
```

jess: Thanks — marking this thread as actionable. I'll attach the KB and request security signoff for bypass. :thumbsup:

customer-ops: thx all, will report back with curl/openssl outputs.
